questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.1 Identify required forklift operator training components
questions.text: What three elements must forklift operator training include?

answers.text: Formal training, practical training, and evaluation of competency
A short quiz, a signature sheet, and permission to practice alone
A manufacturer brochure, a verbal warning, and a timecard entry
A driver’s license, a toolbox talk, and coworker approval

explanations.a: Forklift operator training must include formal instruction, hands-on practical training, and an evaluation of the operator’s competency. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: a quiz or signature alone does not replace practical training and evaluation.
explanations.c: Operator-safety clue: these items do not provide the required combination of training and evaluation.
explanations.d: Documentation review: a driver’s license or coworker approval does not meet forklift operator training requirements.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.1 Identify required forklift operator training components
questions.text: Which activity is an example of formal forklift training?

answers.text: Guessing the controls by watching another operator from a distance
Classroom discussion, lecture, video, or written material covering forklift safety topics
Signing a blank certification card before training begins
Operating a forklift alone in a busy aisle before instruction

explanations.a: Evaluation-requirement review: observation alone is not adequate formal training.
explanations.b: Formal training can include classroom instruction, discussion, videos, written material, or similar instructional methods. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Refresher-trigger check: certification must verify training and evaluation, not precede them.
explanations.d: Trainer-qualification review: unsupervised operation before training creates hazards.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.1 Identify required forklift operator training components
questions.text: During forklift operator certification review, What is practical forklift training?

answers.text: Watching a forklift operate from an office window
Reading only the table of contents from a workbook
Hands-on and site-specific training using the type of truck and workplace conditions involved
Memorizing forklift brand names without operating practice

explanations.a: Practical-training clue: watching from a distance does not provide hands-on skill development.
explanations.b: Competency-check note: reading alone does not provide hands-on practical training.
explanations.c: Practical training gives the operator hands-on instruction related to the equipment and site-specific work. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Workplace-hazard clue: brand memorization does not demonstrate safe operation.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.1 Identify required forklift operator training components
questions.text: Why is competency evaluation required?

answers.text: To replace all future training forever
To allow unsafe operators to keep working if production is busy
To certify the forklift’s mechanical condition
To determine whether the operator can safely operate the forklift

explanations.a: Answer boundary: evaluation does not remove the need for refresher training when required.
explanations.b: Operator-safety clue: unsafe operation must be corrected, not ignored.
explanations.c: Documentation review: operator evaluation is about the operator’s competency, not equipment certification.
explanations.d: Evaluation verifies the operator has the knowledge and practical ability to operate safely. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.2 Recognize employer evaluation and certification requirements
questions.text: What must certification verify?

answers.text: That all workplace hazards have been eliminated
That the operator may use any forklift in any workplace without limits
That the operator has been trained and evaluated to safely operate a forklift
That the forklift will never need maintenance

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.2 Recognize employer evaluation and certification requirements
questions.text: Which information belongs on the certification document?

answers.text: A blank line where all training topics should be listed
The operator’s favorite forklift color
The number of pallets moved during the busiest week
Operator name, trainer name, training and evaluation dates, topics covered, and how training was implemented

explanations.a: Workplace-hazard clue: certification should document the topics covered and implementation.
explanations.b: Truck-type note: color preference is not certification information.
explanations.c: Attachment-training check: production output is not the required certification content.
explanations.d: The workbook lists these items as part of the certification document. This is the correct answer.

explanations.d: Evaluation-requirement review: a supplier does not certify the employer’s operator competency.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.3 Identify when refresher training is required
questions.text: When is refresher training required for a forklift operator?

answers.text: When the operator is observed operating the forklift in an unsafe manner
Solely when the operator changes lunch schedules
Solely when the operator asks for a new uniform
Solely when the forklift paint changes color

explanations.a: Observed unsafe operation is a trigger for refresher training. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: lunch schedule changes are not a forklift training trigger.
explanations.c: Operator-safety clue: uniform requests are unrelated to refresher training.
explanations.d: Documentation review: paint color does not determine refresher training need.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.3 Identify when refresher training is required
questions.text: Which event requires refresher training consideration?

answers.text: The operator takes a normal vacation
The operator is involved in a forklift accident or near-miss incident
The operator receives a new locker assignment
The operator changes personal phone numbers

explanations.a: Evaluation-requirement review: a normal vacation is not listed as a refresher trigger.
explanations.b: An accident or near-miss incident is a refresher training trigger. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Refresher-trigger check: locker assignment does not affect forklift competency.
explanations.d: Trainer-qualification review: phone number changes do not affect forklift operation training.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.3 Identify when refresher training is required
questions.text: During forklift operator certification review, A workplace condition changes in a way that could affect safe forklift operation. What is required?

answers.text: Let operators figure it out during production
Update only the breakroom notice board
Refresher training on the affected safe-operation issues
Ignore the change until the next three-year evaluation

explanations.a: Practical-training clue: operators need training on changed conditions that affect safe operation.
explanations.b: Competency-check note: a notice board does not replace needed refresher training.
explanations.c: Workplace changes that affect safe operation can require refresher training. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Workplace-hazard clue: a safety-affecting change should be addressed before exposure continues.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.3 Identify when refresher training is required
questions.text: An operator is assigned to a different type of forklift or a new attachment. What should happen?

answers.text: Use the old certification without reviewing the change
Assume all forklifts operate exactly the same
Allow operation first and train only if a problem occurs
Provide training for the different forklift or attachment before authorized operation

explanations.a: Answer boundary: certification must reflect the equipment and conditions the operator can safely operate.
explanations.b: Operator-safety clue: different trucks and attachments can change controls, capacity, and stability.
explanations.c: Documentation review: training should occur before exposure to new equipment hazards.
explanations.d: Assignment to a different forklift type or new attachment is a refresher training trigger. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.4 Recognize trainer qualifications and workplace-specific training needs
questions.text: During training, a supervisor is deciding whether an employee may operate a forklift. What qualifications must forklift trainers have?

answers.text: Knowledge, training, and experience necessary to train and evaluate operators
Experience watching forklifts from a distance only
Permission from any coworker regardless of skill
A job title with no forklift safety knowledge

explanations.a: Trainers must have the knowledge, training, and experience needed to train and evaluate forklift operators. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Workplace-hazard clue: trainers need practical knowledge and judgment for safe operation.
explanations.c: Truck-type note: trainer qualification is based on knowledge, training, and experience.
explanations.d: Attachment-training check: a title alone does not prove training capability.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.4 Recognize trainer qualifications and workplace-specific training needs
questions.text: If training is done outside the workplace, what else is needed?

answers.text: A verbal statement that the operator is confident
On-site training covering workplace-specific hazards and tasks
No additional training because all workplaces are identical
Solely a new wallet card with no site instruction

explanations.a: Documentation review: confidence does not replace site-specific training.
explanations.b: Outside training must be supplemented with workplace-specific instruction for the operator’s actual tasks and hazards. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Safe-use logic: forklift hazards and tasks vary by workplace.
explanations.d: Training-component clue: a card does not cover site-specific hazards by itself.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification
questions.objective: 7.4 Recognize trainer qualifications and workplace-specific training needs
questions.text: Why is workplace-specific forklift training important?

answers.text: It lets operators ignore operating instructions
It removes the need for evaluation
Surface conditions, pedestrian traffic, narrow aisles, loads, ramps, and other local hazards vary by site
It applies only to visitors who never operate forklifts

explanations.a: Trainer-qualification review: site training adds to, not replaces, operating instructions.
explanations.b: Site-specific clue: evaluation is still required to determine competency.
explanations.c: Workplace-related topics must reflect the actual environment where the forklift will be operated. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Authorization-decision review: operators need training on the workplace where they will operate.

questions.name: Training, Evaluation, and Certification

questions.text: Which trainer characteristic is most important?

answers.text: Seniority unrelated to forklift operation

Practical skills and judgment necessary to operate forklifts safely

explanations.c: Attachment-training check: speed alone does not show safe judgment.
explanations.d: The workbook states trainer experience should include practical skills and judgment needed for safe operation. This is the correct answer.

questions.text: What if an operator was previously trained on a topic that is appropriate for the current truck and workplace?

questions.text: Which statement best addresses operator authorization and reassignment? Which operator should not be authorized yet?

An operator retrained after unsafe operation and found competent
